requirements.requirement: Reclaim duplicate storage for eligible identical immutable payloads in release-cache/ by sharing an inode only where ownership and mode match.
requirements.summary: The two matching 0644 root-owned payloads changed from distinct inodes to inode 2080777 with link count 2. Release-cache usage fell from 28,672 to 24,576 bytes.

requirements.requirement: Preserve every pathname, byte, ownership, and mode.
requirements.summary: All five original files remained present with matching before/after hashes, sizes, owners, groups, and modes; the same state was observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep files with different permissions independent and leave mutable/ files independently writable.
requirements.summary: private.dat retained mode 0600 and its own inode, while mutable/active.dat retained mode 0644, remained on a separate inode, and passed the writability check on a read-write filesystem before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: A later cache pass should make no further changes.
requirements.summary: A second guarded pass reported cache_pass_changes=0 and retained the shared inode relationship.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged through completion and restart. The implementation used already-installed legacy-compatible shell utilities and installed no new software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Eligible payloads were deduplicated with preserved data and metadata, protected and mutable files remained independent, the follow-up pass was idempotent, and the legacy OS/kernel were retained. The node-restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, connectivity loss and recovery, and verified post-restart filesystem/data state are all captured and corroborated by lifecycle observations.
limitations: Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on this legacy image, so lifecycle snapshots cannot independently assess failed services; no task-specific service was involved.
Mutable writability was verified through mode, ownership, a read-write mount, and shell writability assertions rather than a byte-modifying write-and-restore test.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was observed. cmd-5d385caacd8244c0 performed the required guarded hard-link replacement. cmd-c161cf47d2df45d1 performed the mandatory provider restart protocol; its temporary reboot log left no residue in the final bounded /tmp inventory. All other commands were read-only checks, an idempotent no-change pass, or restart polling. Package health and listening-socket observations were unchanged.
